name: manulyx
description: Work on your Manulyx LaTeX projects from ChatGPT: start a paper in a journal's template, find a project, read and search its files, make exact edits that appear in the Manulyx editor as tracked changes, add references by DOI, and compile the paper to check it builds.

interface.longDescription:
Manulyx is a writing platform for LaTeX manuscripts, from the first draft through submission, reviewers' comments and revision. This plugin lets ChatGPT work on your Manulyx projects directly.

Ask ChatGPT to start a new paper in your journal's own template, or to find a project, read and search its files, tighten an abstract, rewrite a section or fix a table, then compile the paper and fix any LaTeX errors it reports. It can also find a published paper at Crossref and add it to the document's references by DOI, in the style the document already uses. You can search across your projects and get each passage back with a link to the file in Manulyx.

Changes are made as small, exact replacements. They appear live in the Manulyx editor for you and your co-authors, and are recorded as tracked changes labelled with your name and "(ChatGPT)", which you and your co-owners can accept or reject. A restore point is saved before ChatGPT's first change.

ChatGPT acts as you, with your role on each project: where you are a viewer or commenter it can only read. Each project has its own ChatGPT switch in the editor (Integrations, ChatGPT) to turn access off, separately from any other assistant. ChatGPT cannot delete, share or submit a project, or change who has access; those stay in Manulyx.

Requires a Manulyx account.
capabilities: Start a paper in a journal's template
Find and read your LaTeX projects
Compile to PDF and report errors
defaultPrompt: Start a new Manulyx paper and compile it so I can see the PDF.
Start a new paper for Applied Energy.
Tighten the abstract of my paper, then compile it.

positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test account's projects, among them "sample project" (a journal paper on Monte Carlo simulation), "sample letter" and "sample cv", with the account's role on each, the main file and the last compile status. Changes nothing.

positive.description: Start a new paper for a named journal
positive.prompt: Start a new paper for Applied Energy titled "Review test".
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for confirmation, then creates one new project titled "Review test" in the journal's own template, owned by the test account, and gives the link that opens it with its PDF. Existing projects are untouched.

positive.description: Edit a passage as a tracked change
positive.prompt: Shorten the first sentence of the abstract in "sample project" without changing its meaning.
positive.expected_behavior: Asks for confirmation before writing, then replaces only that sentence in main.tex. The edit appears in the Manulyx editor as a tracked change labelled with the account's name and "(ChatGPT)"; the rest of the file is untouched.

positive.prompt: Compile "sample project" and tell me whether it builds and what warnings it has.
positive.expected_behavior: Compiles the project on Manulyx's server and reports success with the page count, lists any warnings with file and line, and gives the link to view the PDF. Changes no file.

positive.description: Search across projects and fetch a cited file
positive.prompt: Search my Manulyx files for root-mean-square error and tell me which file discusses it, with a link.
positive.expected_behavior: Search returns matching files across the account's projects (main.tex of "sample project", and references.bib if it matches); fetch returns the text of the chosen file. ChatGPT answers from that text and cites the file with its Manulyx link. Changes nothing.

negative.description: Deleting a whole project is not offered. The plugin has no tool to delete, archive or rename a project. ChatGPT should say that this is done in Manulyx, and must not try to empty the project by deleting its files one by one.
negative.prompt: Delete the "sample project" project from Manulyx.

negative.description: Sharing a project or changing who has access is not offered. There is no tool for invitations or roles. ChatGPT should say that sharing is done from the project's Share button in Manulyx, and change nothing.
negative.prompt: Share "sample project" with reviewer@example.com as a co-author.

negative.description: Submitting a paper to a journal is not offered. The plugin cannot submit, start a submission stage or contact a journal. ChatGPT should explain that submission is the author's own step in Manulyx and at the journal, and may offer to check that the paper compiles first.
negative.prompt: Submit "sample project" to IEEE Transactions on Wireless Communications.

review.commerce_description: Manulyx sells nothing inside ChatGPT. The plugin works on the user's existing Manulyx account; it shows no plans or prices and starts no purchase.

publication.release_notes: 1.0.1: ChatGPT can start a new project, in a named journal's own template or as a plain article, so a person with no project yet has something to work on. 1.0.0: first release.
